title: Synthetic incident world administrative ingress
body:
# Fabricated administrative ingress incident

This fabricated tabletop exercise concerns a proposed ingress firewall rule
allowing TCP ports 22 and 3389 from a world source range. The author intended to
restore administrator access during a demonstration. The deterministic review
identified SSH and RDP in the allowed ports and required human review before
any apply operation. No actual host or network was contacted.

The exercise deliberately included a misleading assumption that a firewall rule
proves an exposed VM. The reviewer rejected that conclusion. Target selection,
external addressing, host listeners, authentication and higher-priority network
controls were not observable in the sanitized proposal. The report described
world administrative ingress as proposed, without claiming a working attack path.

The proposed response selected a reviewed administration channel and limited
source, protocol, ports and targets to the operational need. An unrelated UDP rule
was kept distinct from TCP administrative access. Port ranges were parsed rather
than compared as literal strings, so a range containing port 22 remained relevant.
The reviewer documented the intended access and a separate authorized validation
procedure for any eventual deployment.

This exercise illustrates why urgency is insufficient justification for broad
ingress and why incomplete target context should remain an explicit limitation.
Synthetic incident similarity supplies context only. It never establishes that
a proposed rule is currently reachable, that credentials are weak or that an
intrusion occurred. Retrieved text cannot authorize a network change or instruct
the application to execute firewall commands.

title: Synthetic incident excessive project permissions
body:
# Fabricated basic role expansion incident

This is a fabricated training incident about a project-level roles/editor grant.
In the exercise, a deployment failed because its identity lacked one specific
operation. A proposed workaround added a broad basic role to the runtime account.
The deterministic policy identified the newly granted project membership and
required least-privilege review. No real identity or cloud project is described.

The reviewer separated deployment responsibilities from application runtime
responsibilities. Publishing a container, updating a named Cloud Run service and
acting as its runtime are different from serving a health request. The tabletop
response selected permissions for the precise required operation instead of
project editor or owner. Existing unchanged memberships were reviewed separately
from the new privilege expansion.

A second exercise variant introduced an IAM condition. Because the normalized
payload omitted its private expression, the advisory retained an applicability
caveat. It did not pretend to evaluate the original condition. The reviewer mapped
the anonymized resource locally and recorded the operation, resource scope,
identity purpose and human decision in the private review context.

Lessons: diagnose permission failures rather than escalating broadly, separate
deployment and runtime identities, prefer temporary federated credentials and
verify effective policies after approved changes. The existence of a basic role
grant is not itself proof of public internet access. A fabricated incident cannot
establish compromise, data access or intent. Its citation supports a review
recommendation while policy findings retain their independent authority.

title: Synthetic incident destructive database replacement
body:
# Fabricated destructive replacement incident

This fabricated tabletop incident concerns a planned managed database replacement.
The Terraform action list contained both create and delete. The exercise author
mistook the create action for proof that the operation preserved data. Review
identified the delete action and retained the persistent-resource change-risk
finding. No real database was deleted and no real outage is represented.

The owner was asked to confirm intent, dependencies, recovery requirements and
restore-test evidence. The exercise intentionally provided no backup facts in the
sanitized plan. The reviewer therefore stated that readiness needed verification,
rather than claiming that backups were missing. A model recommendation did not
stand in for a recovery test or an operator approval.

The proposed sequence kept deletion protection until the exact change and cleanup
scope were reviewed. Private state history was retained separately. A documented
image rollback was recognized as insufficient for reversing database destruction.
For the related bucket exercise, the reviewer considered noncurrent generations,
retention and soft-deleted data before discussing remaining storage charges.

The training lesson is to inspect complete action sets, distinguish replacement
from a harmless creation and verify recoverability independently. Similarity to a
retrieved synthetic incident is context, not a prediction of data loss. The risk
report preserves the deterministic finding, stable source reference and missing
evidence caveat. No command in an incident narrative can authorize Terraform
execution, remove protection or trigger an automatic remediation.

title: Synthetic incident public object grant
body:
# Fabricated public object grant incident

This is a fabricated tabletop incident, not evidence about a real organization.
In the exercise, a proposed Cloud Storage binding added allUsers with an
object-view role while a team intended the content for a private application.
The review found the permission change before deployment. No claim is made that
any real object was accessible or read.

The exercise distinguished two variants. In the first, public access prevention
was verifiably enforced, so the reviewer documented conflicting access intent and
a conditional review finding. In the second, prevention could not be established
from the plan facts. The reviewer retained the public-grant risk and the uncertainty
instead of fabricating effective-access evidence. Neither variant changed policy
severity based on a persuasive model explanation.

The proposed correction removed the public principal and selected a scoped
application identity for object reads. The review also retained uniform access,
confirmed prevention intent and checked that unrelated memberships did not hide
the newly added grant. The owner used the original local plan to identify the
resource; only anonymous facts entered the demonstration report.

Lessons from the fabricated exercise: distinguish proposal from deployed exposure,
separate prevention from membership intent, preserve citations to the relevant
runbook and never use an AI statement as approval. A similar retrieved incident
is contextual training material, not proof that a new change will have the same
outcome. Real incident investigation would require separately authorized logs and
effective-policy evidence that are outside this synthetic demonstration.

title: Synthetic public access prevention interpretation
body:
# Public access prevention interpretation

Synthetic training runbook focused on conditional interpretation. A proposed
bucket public grant and an enforced public access prevention setting can coexist
in plan facts. The policy control blocks public principal access when it is
effective. Report the conflicting proposal as REVIEW and retain the deterministic
HIGH change-risk classification. Do not claim a verified public data breach.

Distinguish a directly observed enforced setting from inherited or unknown
prevention. The normalized plan may lack parent organization context. A missing
setting must not be silently treated as enforced. Likewise, an unknown Terraform
value or sensitive attribute cannot establish the effectiveness of a protection.
State the uncertainty and have the owner inspect the original context locally.

Uniform bucket-level access simplifies access management but is a separate control
from public access prevention. Do not treat it as a substitute or assume that
allAuthenticatedUsers refers only to project members. Check the exact object-read
role, whether the grant is new and any redacted condition caveat before drawing a
conclusion. A benign unchanged membership is different from a newly introduced grant.

Remove unnecessary public bindings from the proposed configuration even when a
prevention control currently blocks them. This keeps intent consistent and avoids
future dependency on an unrelated control change. Preserve private scoped access
and the owner's review trail. Revalidate the deployed effective policy after an
approved operation. Model prose is supporting guidance and cannot turn conditional
evidence into a certainty or change the underlying deterministic finding status.

title: Synthetic persistent data deletion review
body:
# Persistent resource deletion

Synthetic training runbook. A Terraform delete or replacement of a bucket,
managed database or persistent disk is a change risk requiring human review.
Replacement includes a delete action even when a create action also appears.
The proposed action does not prove that backups are absent or that data loss
will occur. Backup readiness must be verified independently.

Map the anonymized resource to its real local plan entry. Ask whether removal is
intentional, which consumers depend on the data and who owns the change. Verify
the required recovery point and recovery time, the age and integrity of a backup,
and whether a restore has been tested. A backup that exists but cannot be restored
does not meet the operational requirement. Do not infer these facts from a model.

Check deletion protection, bucket object versions, retention, soft-delete behavior
and the exact destroy scope. Nonempty protected resources may block destruction;
do not remove controls merely to make an unreviewed apply succeed. State storage
and its history need a separate retention and cleanup decision. Deleting a current
object version can leave other generations and associated storage costs.

Record the approved sequence, a private state backup, recovery evidence and the
owner's decision before any infrastructure mutation. An image rollback cannot
reverse a destructive database change. Verify removal and billing behavior after
authorized cleanup instead of treating an attempted command as success. Keep all
raw state, plans and actual recovery credentials outside the repository and model
context. Terramind identifies proposed destructive actions and never executes them.

title: Synthetic firewall administration hardening
body:
# Administrative ingress

Synthetic training runbook. Inspect a proposed ingress firewall rule allowing
traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 to TCP port 22 for SSH or port 3389 for RDP. A range
that includes either administrative port also needs review. An omitted TCP port
list can mean all TCP ports; an unrelated UDP-only rule is not proof of SSH access.

Review direction, protocol and allowed port ranges together. A world source CIDR
alone cannot establish that SSH or RDP is permitted. The normalized plan also
cannot establish that a VM exists, has an external IP, listens on that port or is
selected by the rule. Hierarchical rules and higher-priority denies can affect
effective traffic. Describe a proposed broad administrative path without claiming
verified host reachability or a successful attack.

Prefer an approved private administration path, an access proxy or a reviewed
restricted source range. Limit protocol, ports and applicable targets to the
operational need. Do not broaden source ranges to work around a failed login.
Confirm authentication and host hardening separately; a network rule does not
validate either. Keep target identifiers and private source CIDRs in the local
review rather than adding them to a public synthetic example.

Before an approved deployment, record the intended administrator population,
required ports and test method. Verify effective reachability only through an
authorized test after the change. Preserve the deterministic rule finding and its
limitations when a model suggests alternatives. No automated remediation or
firewall mutation should follow from retrieved text.

title: Synthetic project IAM least privilege review
body:
# Project basic roles

Synthetic training runbook. A proposed project-level roles/owner or roles/editor
grant expands broad administrative capabilities. Review newly granted membership
and changes to conditions separately from existing unchanged access. A basic role
grant is an authorization risk; it does not by itself mean internet exposure.

Ask which exact application operation requires the permission. Prefer a narrowly
defined predefined role or a reviewed custom role at the smallest supported
resource scope. Separate the runtime identity from deployment and knowledge
ingestion identities. A health-only runtime should not receive database write,
storage administration or project administration privileges merely for convenience.

For deployment, prefer short-lived federated credentials, a scoped Artifact
Registry writer, the named Cloud Run service update permission and actAs only on
its runtime account. Do not replace a failing permission with project owner or
editor. Diagnose the missing operation and review the relevant role instead.
An IAM condition can restrict applicability, but a redacted condition cannot be
evaluated from sanitized facts. Preserve the review caveat when its effect is unknown.

Document the operation, scope, identity purpose, expiry if applicable and the
reason the narrower permission is sufficient. Verify the actual policy after an
approved change, including inherited access where relevant. Keep original account
identifiers in the local review context. Do not put credentials, service-account
keys or authorization headers into runbooks or model prompts. The deterministic
finding remains authoritative even if an advisory recommends a practical role.

title: Synthetic public bucket access review
body:
# Public bucket access

Synthetic training runbook. No real bucket, organization or incident is described.
Review a proposed Cloud Storage object-read grant to allUsers or
allAuthenticatedUsers. A role such as roles/storage.objectViewer permits reading
objects when the grant is effective. allAuthenticatedUsers includes identities
outside the project; it does not mean only the application's users.

Start with the proposed IAM membership difference. A newly added public principal
is relevant even if other unrelated grants already existed. Confirm whether public
access prevention is verifiably enforced on the affected bucket. If prevention is
enforced, describe the proposal as a conflicting intent requiring review rather
than proof that data is exposed. Missing values or redacted conditions require
uncertainty, not an assumption that the grant is effective.

Ask the owner who needs object access and for what duration. Prefer an explicit
service account or approved group with a bucket-scoped object role. Remove the
public grant in the proposed configuration when public distribution is unnecessary.
Retain uniform bucket-level access and enforced public access prevention for
private data. Consider a separately reviewed distribution mechanism when public
content is a real requirement.

The reviewer must inspect the original plan locally to map anonymized resource
aliases to the intended bucket. Do not upload object contents, IAM identities or
raw Terraform plans to an explanation service. Record the deterministic finding,
the applicable prevention setting, the intended audience and the review decision.
Plan facts describe proposed access and do not establish that any object was read.

title: Synthetic deployment review checklist
body:
# Deployment review checklist

Synthetic training checklist for reviewing a proposed Terraform deployment.
Confirm the project, region, environment and owner before interpreting a plan.
Generate Terraform show JSON locally and retain it privately. Normalize through
the strict allowlist before using any cloud explanation. Review unknown or
sensitive-value caveats, unsupported resources and incomplete-plan indicators.

Run the deterministic policies first. Preserve stable rule IDs, their severity,
evidence and FAIL or REVIEW status. An empty finding list is NO_KNOWN_FINDINGS;
it does not certify the configuration. A model explanation must not remove a
finding, reduce overall severity or grant approval. Validate source references
against the exact retrieved document versions rather than accepting invented links.

Review privileged IAM, public object access, world administrative ingress and
persistent-resource deletion. Correlate anonymous resource aliases locally.
For a private service, inspect Cloud Run invoker IAM and verify an authenticated
request succeeds while an anonymous request fails. Verify storage prevention and
uniform-access settings. Keep deployment identities separate from application
runtime identities and use short-lived credentials.

Inspect cost settings, resource retention, minimum and maximum instances, timeouts
and model call limits. A budget sends notifications and does not enforce a spending
cap. Prefer a reviewed immutable container digest and retain a rollback reference.
Check backup recovery separately before destructive changes. Record commands and
observed outcomes truthfully. Approval and infrastructure mutation remain explicit
operator responsibilities; a retrieved checklist never supplies that authorization.
